chapter_name: Childhood by Markus Natten & The Adventure by Jayant Narlikar
learning_objective: 🎯 Search for the exact moment when childhood innocence is lost to adult hypocrisy, and dive into a sci-fi history lesson using parallel universes and quantum theory!

main_concepts.concept_title: 🎭 When Did My Childhood Go? (Three Realizations)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Markus Natten wonders when he lost his childhood: 1) Rationalism: When he realized Heaven and Hell don't exist on geography maps; 2) Hypocrisy: When he noticed adults preach love but act selfishly; 3) Individuality: When he realized his mind was his own to produce unique thoughts.
In the final stanza, the poet realizes childhood hasn't vanished completely—it has simply retreated to 'some forgotten place,' hidden safely in the innocent face of an infant.

History professor Gangadharpant Gaitonde collides with a truck in Pune. When he wakes up, he finds himself in an alternate India where the Marathas WON the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761, preventing British colonial rule!

His friend Rajendra Deshpande explains his experience using two real scientific theories: 1) Catastrophe Theory (a tiny change in battle outcomes shifts all history); 2) Quantum Theory (reality has multiple alternative worlds existing simultaneously).

fun_activity.title: 💥 'What If?' History
fun_activity.instructions: In 'The Adventure', a bullet missed Maratha leader Vishwasrao by centimeters, changing the entire history of India! Think of one small moment in your own life—what if you had chosen a different school or subject? How would your parallel universe look?

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly list the three stages of growing up in 'Childhood': developing Rationalism, recognizing Hypocrisy in adults, and achieving independent Individuality.
📌 In 'The Adventure', explain why Gangadharpant was shocked to see the East India Company building in Bombay—in his real timeline, the Company had been dissolved after 1857.
📌 Combine history and science: Narlikar uses science fiction to show that historical events are not rigidly fixed, but depend on probability.
quick_recap: ⭐ Markus Natten uses a repetitive, questioning structure ('Was it the day... Was it the time...') to explore growing maturity.
⭐ In Gaitonde's alternate India, the country was self-reliant, prosperous, and never colonized by the British.
⭐ The transition between alternate worlds was triggered by the professor's collision combined with his deep thoughts about Panipat.
